title: Reformat Department Table
statement:
One table stores monthly revenue per department, one fact per row:

- `Department(id, revenue, month)`: department `id` earned `revenue` in `month`. The pair `(id, month)` is unique, so a department has at most one row per month. `month` is one of `Jan`, `Feb`, `Mar`, `Apr`, `May`, `Jun`, `Jul`, `Aug`, `Sep`, `Oct`, `Nov`, `Dec`.

Turn the months into columns: output one row per department that appears in the table, with 13 columns in this order: `id`, then `Jan_Revenue`, `Feb_Revenue`, `Mar_Revenue`, `Apr_Revenue`, `May_Revenue`, `Jun_Revenue`, `Jul_Revenue`, `Aug_Revenue`, `Sep_Revenue`, `Oct_Revenue`, `Nov_Revenue` and `Dec_Revenue`. Each month column holds that department's revenue for the month, or `null` when the department has no row for it (not 0). Rows may come in any order.
constraints: month is one of Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec
id and month are never null
reference:
SELECT id,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Jan' THEN revenue END) AS Jan_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Feb' THEN revenue END) AS Feb_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Mar' THEN revenue END) AS Mar_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Apr' THEN revenue END) AS Apr_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'May' THEN revenue END) AS May_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Jun' THEN revenue END) AS Jun_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Jul' THEN revenue END) AS Jul_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Aug' THEN revenue END) AS Aug_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Sep' THEN revenue END) AS Sep_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Oct' THEN revenue END) AS Oct_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Nov' THEN revenue END) AS Nov_Revenue,
       SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'Dec' THEN revenue END) AS Dec_Revenue
FROM Department
GROUP BY id;
brute:
SELECT d.id,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Jan') AS Jan_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Feb') AS Feb_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Mar') AS Mar_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Apr') AS Apr_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'May') AS May_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Jun') AS Jun_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Jul') AS Jul_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Aug') AS Aug_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Sep') AS Sep_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Oct') AS Oct_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Nov') AS Nov_Revenue,
  (SELECT revenue FROM Department WHERE id = d.id AND month = 'Dec') AS Dec_Revenue
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM Department) AS d
notes:
## Intuition

The input is "long" (one row per department and month) and the output is "wide" (one row per department, one column per month). Long-to-wide is a **pivot**, and in MySQL a pivot is a `GROUP BY` plus one conditional aggregate per output column. Grouping by `id` makes one output row per department. Inside a group, `CASE WHEN month = 'Jan' THEN revenue END` keeps the January revenue and turns every other row into `null`; `SUM` ignores nulls, so it returns that one revenue, or `null` when the department has no January row at all.

## Approach

1. Read `Department` and `GROUP BY id`, giving one group per department.
2. For each of the 12 months, write `SUM(CASE WHEN month = '<Mon>' THEN revenue END)` and name it `<Mon>_Revenue`.
3. Select `id` first, then the twelve month columns from `Jan_Revenue` to `Dec_Revenue`.

## Example 1, step by step

- Group `id = 1` holds (8000, Jan), (7000, Feb), (6000, Mar). The Jan expression sees 8000, null, null and sums to 8000; Feb gives 7000; Mar gives 6000; Apr through Dec see only nulls and give `null`.
- Group `id = 2` holds (9000, Jan): `Jan_Revenue = 9000`, every other month `null`.
- Group `id = 3` holds (10000, Feb): `Feb_Revenue = 10000`, every other month `null`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(R) for R rows: one grouping pass, with 12 cheap expressions per row.
- Space: O(D) for D departments in the result.

## Pitfalls

- `CASE ... ELSE 0 END` (or `IFNULL(..., 0)`) reports 0 for missing months; the answer needs `null` there.
- Selecting `revenue` directly without an aggregate is not valid under `ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY` and picks one arbitrary month.
- Every one of the 13 column names must match exactly, including the capital `R` in `_Revenue` and the three-letter month codes such as `Sep`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `GROUP BY id` | one output row per department |
| `CASE WHEN month = 'Jan' THEN revenue END` | the row's revenue if it is the January row, otherwise `null` |
| `SUM(...)` | the single matching revenue, or `null` if none |
| `Jan_Revenue` ... `Dec_Revenue` | the twelve month columns |

narration.1: Each output row starts with the department id.
narration.2: CASE keeps a row's revenue only if it is the January row; SUM over the group returns it, or null when there is none.
narration.7: The same pattern repeats for every month; only the month code and the column name change.
narration.13: December is the last of the twelve conditional columns.
narration.15: Grouping by id collapses each department's month rows into a single output row.
